course_title: Communication and Feeding Skills in Children II
course_description: This course introduces students to the planning and implementation of evidence-based interventions for communication and feeding/mealtime management difficulties that can present in children under five years of age. Practical activities foster the development and demonstration of critical reflection and clinical reasoning and knowledge of the role of other professions in the overall management of communication disorders and feeding/mealtime difficulties in children under five years of age.

course_aims:
This course is a follow-on course from SPCH7111. In this course, students will develop skills in collaborative goal setting and planning and implementation of evidence-based interventions for communication and/or feeding/mealtime difficulties experienced by children under five years of age. Online self-directed learning activities are supplemented by tutorials in which students will engage in peer-to-peer learning activities to gain experience in critical reflection and clinical reasoning and the ethical provision of person and family-centred services to children under five years of age from diverse backgrounds. Through active engagement in authentic learning opportunities, students will develop an understanding of the role of interprofessional teams in the overall management of communication and feeding/mealtime management difficulties in young children.

This course offers students a flipped approach to learning. Students engage in online learning resources before weekly tutorials where they then participate in authentic learning experiences with peers and teaching staff. In the tutorials, students engage in peer-to-peer learning through active participation in independent, small group and large group inquiry-based learning activities. This provides students with more flexibility to learn, but the associated workload is similar to that of a traditional course.

learning_outcomes.description: Collaborate with families and significant others to develop relevant communication and/or feeding goals for children under five years of age (Speech Pathology Australia Professional Standards, Domains/Standards 1.4, 1.6, 1.7, 2.5, 3.1 and 3.4)

Plan and implement holistic and evidence-based intervention for communication and/or feeding difficulties experienced by children under five years of age. (SPA PS Domains/Standards 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.4, 1.5, 1.6, 2.5, 2.6, 3.1, 3.4 and 3.5)

Demonstrate critical reflection and clinical reasoning in providing person- and family-centred services to children under five years of age and their significant others. (SPA PS Domains/Standards 1.4, 1.6, 2.2, 2.5, 3.3 and 3.5)

Explain how to uphold the Code of Ethics when managing children under five years of age with communication and/or feeding difficulties and their families. (SPA PS Domains/Standards 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, and 1.5)

Develop a culturally responsive intervention plan for children under five years of age who are from an Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander background and their families. (SPA PS Domains/Standards 1.3, 1.4, 1.5, 1.6, 1.7, 2.1, 2.5, 2.6, 3.1, 3.3 and 3.4)
Analyse the role of interprofessional teams in the overall management of communication and feeding difficulties in children under five years of age. (SPA PS Domains/Standards 1.4, 1.7, 2.6 and 3.4)

Demonstrate the ability to work effectively in an interprofessional team, alongside speech pathology and social work colleagues, towards a common goal. (SPA PS Domains/Standards 1.4, 1.5, 2.5, 2.6, 3.1 and 3.4)

Recognise and demonstrate interprofessional collaboration skills including role clarification and negotiation, team functioning and communication (trust, accountability, inclusion, psychological safety), underpinned by relationship-focused-care and services (SPA PS Domains/Standards – 1.4, 1.5, 2.2, 2.5, 2.6, 3.1 and 3.4).

assessment_details.title: GEMS IPCP Curriculum Assessment
assessment_details.task_description: Inter Professional Collaborative Practice (IPCP) Curriculum Assessment The assessment will be completed in your timetabled tutorial class, with a final submission date set a week later. This is a team assessment, and all team members are expected to contribute equally to the team’s assessment items during the tutorial. Teams will be assigned prior to the tutorial. There are two (2) parts to this assessment – a worksheet based upon a client video that your team will choose during the tutorial class, and a team check in with your tutor. Part One requires you to complete a worksheet and will draw on the content of the GEMS IPCP module one, focusing on role-clarification and negotiation, team communication, team functioning, and relationship focused care and services: Length: There is no word limit for the worksheet. Part Two involves a check-in with a tutor, to assess and reflect on processes of collaboration. Length : approx. 10 minutes Teams will need to submit Part One in the Assessment tab on the IPCP Learn.UQ course site at the end of the tutorial class. Additional information regarding submission will be provided on the HABS1240 GEMS IPCP Learn.UQ course site. Please refer to the assessment information on Learn.UQ for further details and requirements for the assessment. assessment_details.submission_guidelines:
The IPCP module is a Pass/Fail assessment task. Students who pass the module will receive a course grade based on their passing the remaining must pass assessment/s in the course.
Students who are unable to attend the module on the day of the tutorial class (due to illness, placement or extenuating circumstances), who are unable to reschedule to a subsequent tutorial, will be given an opportunity to complete an individual assessment. Successful completion of the assessment will again enable a PASS grade for the module. For all students who submit a genuine attempt at the assessment but do not achieve a pass grade for their submitted work, they will be given a second opportunity to pass the module by completing a reflective essay. If this task is successfully completed, a grade for the course will be awarded based on the remaining assessment in the course. Students who do not engage with the module and do not submit a genuine attempt, will be given an opportunity to complete a 5,000 word assignment on teamwork. Successful completion of this assignment will enable the student to be eligible to pass the course with a maximum grade of 4 (if the remaining assessment in the course would result in a grade higher than 4, a maximum grade of 4 will be awarded). Students who fail the module, who do not complete either the reflective essay or the teamwork assignment above will be awarded a maximum grade of 3 (if the remaining assessment in the course would result in a grade higher than 3, a maximum grade of 3 will be awarded).

assessment_details.task_description: Students will participate in one 2-hour practical session focused on paediatric feeding, designed to support the development of skills in managing paediatric dysphagia. During the session, they will complete a series of part tasks (e.g., infant oral reflex examination, positioning, cue reading, and use of feeding equipment) and engage in a simulated interaction with the caregiver of a child experiencing feeding difficulties. assessment_details.title: Holistic management case presentation
assessment_details.category: Paper/ Report/ Annotation, Presentation, Role play/ Simulation
assessment_details.task_description: This is an authentic, group-based assessment that allows you to bring together the theory gained in the course and apply it collaboratively to a case. You will be provided with case information and case data for a young child (0-5 years) presenting with communication and/or swallowing difficulties. Working in a clinical team, you will be required to (a) develop a written intervention plan identifying further assessment, referral, and intervention priorities for this case; and (b) deliver a prerecorded discussion simulating a case conference presentation, in which your team discusses and justifies your clinical decision-making and demonstrates the practical application of selected intervention strategies. Throughout this assessment, you will be expected to draw on evidence-based practice, person- and family-centred care approaches, and alignment with the Professional Standards for Speech Pathologists in Australia (2020) and the Speech Pathology Australia Code of Ethics (2020). Each member of the group will receive the same mark on the completion of the case presentation criteria (15%). Teamwork scores (i.e., Buddycheck) will be based on peer-assessment of group member contributions to the assessment (5%). A detailed task description and marking criteria will be made available on the course Blackboard site. learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From O-week To Week 1 (20 Jul - 02 Aug)
learning_activities.topic: GEMS Interprofessional Collaborative Practice Module GEMS Interprofessional Collaborative Practice Module 1 x Tutorial – 3 hours You will work in small teams in the tutorial with students from: Audiology, Dentistry, Dietetics, Nursing, Occupational Therapy, Physiotherapy, Psychology, Social Work and Speech Pathology. There is one module consisting of on-line preparation and a face-to-face tutorial class. You will work in your small team to engage in a range of learning activities to develop your knowledge and skills to help prepare you for working in interprofessional collaborative teams when caring for clients. Learning outcomes: L08

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 1 To Week 12 (27 Jul - 25 Oct)
learning_activities.topic: Online self-directed learning modules (self-directed learning) A series of weekly online lectures/modules will provide information on the holistic management of communication and feeding/mealtime difficulties in children under five years of age. The self-directed learning content will cover a broad range of topics, including family-centred care and cultural capability frameworks, goal-setting, prevention and promotion of communication difficulties in young children, neurodiversity and neurodivergence, and the management of predominant difficulties observed in children under five years of age (e.g., language, literacy, speech, voice, fluency, and feeding).

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 1 To Week 12 (27 Jul - 25 Oct)
learning_activities.topic: Weekly on campus tutorials Tutorials will be conducted from weeks 1-8, 10 and 12 of the semester, and will incorporate inquiry-based learning and small group discussion to further explore early speech pathology approaches to the management of communication and feeding/mealtime difficulties in children under five years of age. Tutorials have been designed for experiential learning and therefore, students are expected to attend and participate in all tutorials. It is essential that students prepare for tutorials by completing the online self-paced learning modules and associated preparation activities. As students will be working in small groups during this learning activity, tutorials will not be recorded.
Introductory lecture The introductory lecture (week 1) will provide an overview of speech pathology management of communication and feeding/mealtime difficulties in young children.

Fluency Practical In Week 2, students will participate in a paediatric fluency practical session in place of their regular tutorial. This session will use inquiry-based learning and small group discussions to deepen understanding of early speech pathology management for fluency/stuttering difficulties in children under five years old. To make the most of this session, students must complete the online self-paced learning module and related preparation activities beforehand. As this is a small-group, interactive activity, it will not be recorded.

Interprofessional workshop Students will participate in one (1) interprofessional workshop with Social Work students. This workshop will be held on campus and will not be recorded. Attendance is highly encouraged.

Supporting neurodivergent children and families workshop In Week 11, an organisation specialised in supporting autistic children and families will deliver a workshop focused on supporting the communication needs of neurodivergent children. The session will provide practical strategies and insights to enhance inclusive and effective communication across clinical and educational settings. Attendance is highly encouraged as this learning activity will not be recorded. Note. This workshop will be timetabled outside regular tutorial hours.

Paediatric Feeding Practical On Friday in Week 11, students will participate in one 2-hour practical activity focused on paediatric feeding, designed to support the development of skills in managing paediatric dysphagia. During the session, students will complete a series of part tasks (e.g., infant oral reflex examination, positioning, cue reading, and use of feeding equipment) and engage in a simulated interaction with the caregiver of a child experiencing feeding difficulties. Attendance is highly encouraged as this learning activity will not be recorded.

Final lecture The final lecture will be pre-recorded and released in Week 13. This lecture will review the course and provide direction for knowledge translation into later courses and future learning activities in the program.
